q: Internal stimuli or internal control are chemicals called plant ____. (2026- Set 1)
e: Plant hormones act as chemical messengers that regulate growth and physiological responses to internal stimuli.

q: Plants lack a ____ system like animals. (2025- Set 7)
e: Unlike animals, plants do not possess a nervous system and rely on chemical signaling for coordination.

q: Plants can respond to their ____ in various ways. (2024-ရန်ကုန်နှင့်တိုင်းခရိုင်အချို့တွင်မေး / 2025-Set 10)
e: Plants adapt and modify their growth patterns in response to environmental changes.

q: In generals, growth is considered as an ____ in size of the object. (2025- Set 3)
e: Biological growth is defined as an irreversible increase in the overall size or mass of an organism.

q: Some special chemical substances regulate growth and development in plants are called plant hormones or ____. (2025- Set 12)
e: Phytohormones are organic chemical regulators produced naturally within plant tissues.

q: Application of auxin to unpollinated pistil makes them develop seedless fruits or ____. (2025- Set 11/2026-နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: Parthenocarpy refers to the formation of seedless fruits without prior fertilization.

q: Phytohormones are essential ____ compounds required in very small quantities. (2025- Set 7)
e: Phytohormones are organic compounds that regulate growth and development at minute concentrations.

q: Some special chemical substances regulate growth and ____ in plants. (2025- Set 9)
e: Plant hormones coordinate both qualitative developmental changes and quantitative cellular growth.

q: Special chemical substances are called plant hormones or ____. (2025- Set 2)
e: Phytohormones is the specific term for endogenous plant growth regulators.

q: Abscisin is an example in the group of hormones that promote ____ in plants. (2025- Set 6)
e: Abscisic acid maintains dormancy in seeds and buds to help plants survive adverse conditions.

q: Abscisic acid acts as ____ of all growth promoters. (2025- Set 4)
e: Abscisic acid acts as an antagonist by opposing the growth-promoting actions of auxins and gibberellins.

q: Auxin initiates and promotes cell division in vascular ____. (2024-Set 3)
e: Auxins stimulate secondary thickening growth by inducing cell division in the vascular cambium.

q: Gibberellins are ____ hormones that include gibberellic acid. (2024-နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: Gibberellins are a class of plant hormones that control stem elongation and seed germination.

q: Coconut milk is a rich source of ____. (2024- Set 2, Set 4)
e: Coconut endosperm contains abundant cytokinins, which stimulate active cell division.

q: Ethylene is the only ____ phytohormone. (2024-နောက်ဆက်တွဲမေးခွန်း)
e: Ethylene is unique among plant hormones because it exists as a gas at physiological temperatures.

q: Epigeal germination takes place ____ the ground. (2026- Set 2)
e: In epigeal germination, hypocotyl elongation raises the cotyledons above the soil surface.

q: Seed germinates in ____ conditions. (2025- Set 1)
e: Seed germination requires favorable environmental conditions such as moisture, oxygen, and temperature.

q: Seed absorbs water through ____ and softens the seed coat. (2025- Set 5)
e: Water enters through the micropyle, causing the seed to swell and soften the outer coat.

q: The germination of seeds inside the fruit, which is still attached to the parent tree is called ____. (2025- Set 8)
e: Vivipary describes the germination of seeds while still contained within fruits attached to the parent plant.

q: Phytochrome is a protein containing covalently attached ____. (2025- Set 13)
e: Phytochrome relies on a light-absorbing chromophore pigment group to detect red and far-red light.

q: A change in the environment which can be detected by the body is called ____. (2024-Set 3 / 2025-Set 10)
e: A stimulus is any detectable change in an organism's external or internal environment.

q: Coordination involves two main ____ systems. (2024-နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: Animal coordination requires interaction between body systems, primarily the nervous and endocrine systems.

q: The delicate tissues of the spinal cord are protected by ____ fluid, soft tissue layers, and the spinal column. (2026- နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: Cerebrospinal fluid provides mechanical protection and cushioning for the brain and spinal cord.

q: Injury to the spinal column can also damage the spinal cord, resulting in ____. (2026-Set 1)
e: Severe spinal cord damage disrupts sensory and motor nerve signals, leading to paralysis.

q: The forebrain comprises the ____, thalamus and hypothalamus. (2026-Set 1)
e: The forebrain consists of the cerebrum together with the thalamus and hypothalamus.

q: The hindbrain consists of the ____, pons and medulla oblongata. (2025- Set 2,11)
e: The hindbrain comprises the cerebellum, pons, and medulla oblongata.

q: Reflex arcs are simple connections of only three ____ to transmit message. (2025- Set 5)
e: A basic reflex arc links three neurones to route impulses rapidly from receptor to effector.

q: The sympathetic neurones release a neurotransmitter called ____. (2025- Set 6)
e: Sympathetic neurons release norepinephrine to prepare the body for stress and action.

q: The forebrain comprises the ____, thalamus and hypothalamus in the brain. (2025- Set 9)
e: The cerebrum forms the dominant anterior part of the forebrain.

q: The skull forms a protective bony ____ around the brain. (2024-Set 4) (2024-ရန်ကုန်နှင့်တိုင်းခရိုင်အချို့တွင်မေး / 2025-Set 1)
e: The cranial bones of the skull form a hard bony armour protecting the brain.

q: The ____ forms a protective bony armour around the brain. (2024-Set 2)
e: The skull encloses and shields the central tissues of the brain from physical injury.

q: Individual neurones are organized into ____ called nerves. (2025- Set 3)
e: Nerves are biological tissues composed of bundles of individual neuronal fibers.

q: The ____ conducts impulses away from the cell body. (2025- Set 4)
e: An axon is the neuronal extension that transmits action potentials away from the soma.

q: Three main types of neurons are sensory neurones, ____ and motor neurones. (2024-နောက်ဆက်တွဲမေးခွန်း)
e: Interneurones connect sensory inputs to motor outputs within the central nervous system.

q: Chemical messengers called ____ carry the neutral signal from one neurone to another. (2025- Set 8,12)
e: Neurotransmitters are chemical signals that convey nerve impulses across synaptic junctions.

q: Sense organs are ____ in which sensory receptors are highly concentrated. (2026- Set 2) (2025- Set 13)
e: Sense organs contain dense clusters of specialized receptor cells to detect stimuli.

q: In bright light, the ____ is constricted. (2025- Set 13)
e: The pupil constricts in high ambient light to reduce the amount of light entering the eye.
